predecessors.name: Kingdom of Lombardy–Venetia
predecessors.text: Venice and most of Venetia, seized from the Austrian kingdom in March 1848

successors.name: Kingdom of Lombardy–Venetia
successors.text: Venice, surrendered to Radetzky in August 1849

ledger.x: 22 March 1848: Daniele Manin proclaims the Republic of San Marco at Venice.
March 1848: the Veneto towns join Venice.
22-23 April 1848: Udine surrenders to Nugent's Austrians.
11-24 June 1848: the mainland towns fall to Austria.
4 July 1848: the Venetian assembly votes union with Sardinia, so Venice passes under the Sardinian crown.
9 August 1848: the union ends and Venice is independent again (the land returns from Sardinia).

By 9 August 1848 Venice alone was held by the insurgents ('the only city in Lombardy-Venetia which remained in the hands of the insurgents'); the page does not date the return of Rovigo, so this event bridges the silence.
13 October 1848: Osoppo, the last mainland stronghold, falls.
22-27 August 1849: Venice surrenders after famine and cholera.
August 1849: the Republic of San Marco ends.

wars.name: Siege of Venice (1849)
wars.outcome: Austria blockaded Venice after the assembly voted on 2 April 1849 to keep fighting, attacked Fort Marghera on 4 May (evacuated 26 May), and Venice capitulated on 22 August (terms) with Radetzky's entry on 27 August 1849.

wars.name: First Italian War of Independence
wars.outcome: The Veneto towns rose in March 1848 and were retaken by Austria in June; Venice held out to August 1849.

certainty.note: The mainland towns changed hands week by week and no frontier text exists; only the Venetian lagoon is a firm outline.
